inputs: backing overhang per side (2, 3, 4 or 6 in; default 4)
batting overhang per side (2, 3 or 4 in; default 4)
seam allowance (1/4 or 1/2 in options; default 1/2)
qualified.outputs: Backing yardage rounded up to 1/8 yd, panel count and cut length, seam direction, batting dimensions with nearest precut name, a 108 in wide-back comparison, optional cost, and a diagram.
qualified.formula: Backing size = quilt size + 2 x overhang on each dimension. Usable width = fabric width minus 2 in selvage. One panel if the backing dimension fits within usable width; otherwise panels = ceil(dimension / (usable width minus 2 x seam allowance)). Both seam directions are compared and the smaller yardage is chosen (panels x cut length / 36), rounded up to the next 1/8 yd. Batting = quilt size + 2 x batting overhang, matched against a precut list. Read from the page's public /assets/calc.js.
qualified.how_to_drive: DOM ids: w (quilt width), l (quilt length), oh (backing overhang select), bo (batting overhang select), fw (fabric width select), sa (seam allowance select), price. Results update live from the inputs; no separate calculate button was seen.

qualified.outputs: Strip count, yardage rounded up to 1/8 yd, join count, cost, strip layout diagram.
qualified.formula: Perimeter = 2 x (width + length); add 4 x strip width + 10 in for corners and closing join. Usable width = fabric width minus 2 in. Strip count is solved iteratively, adding strip width + 0.5 in loss per join. Yardage = strips x strip width / 36, rounded up to 1/8 yd. Bias branch uses a square-area estimate with a waste factor.
qualified.how_to_drive: DOM ids: bqW, bqL, btype, bsw, bfw, bprice; two buttons (primary and ghost) whose ids were not captured. Default values bqW=70, bqL=90.

qualified.outputs: Number of strips and total yardage.
qualified.formula: Per the page text: perimeter = 2 x width + 2 x length, plus 12 extra inches, divided by usable width (fabric width minus 0.5 in) to get strips; yardage = strips x strip width / 36, rounded up to the nearest increment (increment not found). Compiled Next.js app, so the code was not read to confirm.

qualified.found_by: A candidate of the extended border query above and the sibling page named in the backing entry; the driver reaches it from the site's home page link. The access date is that of its driven records (UTC timestamps 2026-10-09T01:39Z to 01:43Z, n = 18, all returning values).
inputs: up to three borders, each with an enable checkbox and a width (in); border 2 starts enabled at 6 in
qualified.outputs: Per enabled border, its yardage and the quilt size after it.
qualified.formula: As modeled in calc_rules.qc_border, which reproduces all 19 compared values: strips = ceil((2 W + 2 L + 4 b + 12) / (fabric width - 1/2)); yards = strips x (b + 1/2) / 36, rounded up to 1/8 yd; each later border sees W and L grown by 2 b.
qualified.how_to_drive: drive.mjs finds the URL from the home page's border link and matches fields by role and label; results update live.

qualified.outputs: Yardage to buy, cutting instruction, strip count, binding length, perimeter.
qualified.formula: Per the page text: perimeter plus an overage allowance, divided by fabric width for strips, strips x cut width / 36 for yards. Rounding increment and overage default not found.
qualified.how_to_drive: Input ids: quilt-width, quilt-height, strip-width, fabric-width, overage (type=number).

qualified.outputs: Strip cut width, number of strips, yardage rounded up to 1/8 yd, with straight and mitered variants (formula fields in a WordPress Forminator form).
qualified.formula: Cut strip width = finished width + 0.5 in (1/4 in seam on each side). Border lengths use quilt size + 2 x border width + 1 in, plus 2 in extra for the other pair. Strip count = ceil of required length (with a doubling factor) over fabric width; yardage = strips x cut width / 36, rounded up to 1/8 yd. Page says strips are joined end to end, not on the diagonal. Exact mitered branch not fully decoded.
qualified.how_to_drive: Forminator fields name=number-1 (quilt width), number-2 (quilt length), number-4 (fabric width, value 42), number-5 (border finished width); computed fields calculation-1 through calculation-12 update from them via data-formula. The id suffix _6ac6ede3c4019 is page specific.

qualified.outputs: Yardage required (to nearest 1/8 yd, rounded up) and number of strips.
qualified.formula: strips = ceil(2 x length / fabricWidth + 2 x (width + borderWidth) / fabricWidth); yardage = strips x borderWidth / fabricWidth, then rounded up to 1/8 yd. No seam allowance and no join loss; the yardage term divides by fabric width, so it follows a different convention from the strip-cut formulas above.
qualified.how_to_drive: Inline JS function calculateFabric() reads ids quiltWidth, quiltLength, borderWidth, fabricWidth; button type=button onclick=calculateFabric(); output id result.

qualified.outputs: Backing and batting amounts in yards and inches or meters and centimeters.
qualified.formula: Page states 4 in is added on every side (8 in on width and length). Directional fabric: bolt width runs along quilt width; if the quilt width exceeds one bolt but fits in two, two pieces of quilt length are used; yardage = pieces x length / 36. Rounding and seam loss not found. Page does not cover binding or borders.
